claims.head: Cole and Vlasic get the Panarin assignment
claims.call: The Blackhawks’ P2 (Cole and Vlasic) spends at least 62% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Cole and Vlasic out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been picking a defense pair for the other team’s top line. Tonight the Kings’ first line is Panarin, Laferriere and Kempe.

claims.gist: At home, Jeff Blashill likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ first line.

claims.head: Tired legs for the Kings
claims.body: It’s the Kings’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Blackhawks get more of the play than usual.
claims.call: The Blackhawks get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.

notes.text: Kevin Fiala is on injured reserve (lower-leg surgery) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Alex Turcotte is on injured reserve and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Quinton Byfield is day to day (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Alex Laferriere has taken his spot beside Adrian Kempe and Artemi Panarin.
Jared Wright was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Joel Armia and Scott Laughton.
Jared Wright was added to the roster on Oct 22 and has played beside Joel Armia and Scott Laughton.
Bowen Byram is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov.
Dominic Toninato was added to the roster on Oct 14 and has played beside Ryan Donato and Oliver Moore.
Artyom Levshunov is no longer playing on the power play: 4% of the team’s power-play time in 10 games, down from 59% last season.

CHI.head: The Blackhawks have a hill to climb
CHI.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage and Los Angeles may be without Byfield, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

LAK.head: Advantage, the Kings
LAK.body: Even though Chicago has home-ice advantage and Los Angeles may be without Byfield, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blackhawks’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blackhawks are 3-7-0. The Kings have won two in a row. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings.
At home, Jeff Blashill likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ first line. The Kings played last night; the Blackhawks are rested.
